ex:AminoAcid.comment: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins.
ex:AminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: An AminoAcid is a MaterialEntity that contains both an amino group and a carboxyl group.

ex:EssentialAminoAcid.comment: These amino acids are crucial for protein synthesis and overall health.
ex:EssentialAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: An EssentialAminoAcid is a MaterialEntity that must be obtained through diet as it cannot be synthesized by the body.

ex:NonEssentialAminoAcid.comment: These amino acids are produced within the body.
ex:NonEssentialAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A NonEssentialAminoAcid is a MaterialEntity that can be synthesized by the body.

ex:SemiEssentialAminoAcid.comment: These amino acids require dietary supplementation.
ex:SemiEssentialAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A SemiEssentialAminoAcid is a MaterialEntity that can be synthesized by the body but in insufficient amounts.

ex:AlphaAminoAcid.comment: The most common type of amino acid.
ex:AlphaAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: An AlphaAminoAcid is a MaterialEntity that has both an amino and carboxyl group attached to the alpha carbon.

ex:DecarboxylationReaction.comment: Involves the removal of a carboxyl group.
ex:DecarboxylationReaction.aristotelian_definition: A DecarboxylationReaction is a Process that converts an amino acid into an amine and carbon dioxide.

ex:Zwitterion.comment: Characterized by the presence of an amino group and a carboxyl group.
ex:Zwitterion.aristotelian_definition: A Zwitterion is a MaterialEntity that contains both positive and negative ionic groups.

ex:NinhydrinReaction.comment: Involves the reaction of ninhydrin with amino groups.
ex:NinhydrinReaction.aristotelian_definition: A NinhydrinReaction is a Process that identifies amino acids through color change.

ex:AliphaticAminoAcid.comment: Includes amino acids like glycine, alanine, valine, leucine, and isoleucine.
ex:AliphaticAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: An AliphaticAminoAcid is an AminoAcid with a side chain that consists of carbon atoms in open chains or unbranched rings.

ex:HydroxylGroupContainingAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A HydroxylGroupContainingAminoAcid is an AminoAcid with a hydroxyl group (-OH) attached to its side chain.

ex:SulphurContainingAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A SulphurContainingAminoAcid is an AminoAcid with a sulfur-containing side chain.

ex:BasicAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A BasicAminoAcid is an AminoAcid with a side chain that has basic properties.

ex:AromaticAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: An AromaticAminoAcid is an AminoAcid with a side chain that contains aromatic rings.

ex:IminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: An IminoAcid is an AminoAcid with a side chain that contains an imino group (=NH) instead of the usual amino group (-NH2).

ex:BetaAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A BetaAminoAcid is an AminoAcid with the amino group attached to the beta carbon.

ex:GammaAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A GammaAminoAcid is an AminoAcid with the amino group attached to the gamma carbon.

ex:PurelyKetogenicAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A PurelyKetogenicAminoAcid is an AminoAcid that can only be metabolized to produce ketone bodies.

ex:KetogenicAndGlucogenicAminoAcid.comment: Includes lysine, isoleucine, phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan.
ex:KetogenicAndGlucogenicAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A KetogenicAndGlucogenicAminoAcid is an AminoAcid that can be metabolized to produce both ketone bodies and glucose.

ex:PurelyGlucogenicAminoAcid.comment: Includes alanine, aspartic acid, glutamic acid, etc.
ex:PurelyGlucogenicAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A PurelyGlucogenicAminoAcid is an AminoAcid that can only be metabolized to produce glucose or glycogen.

ex:NonPolarAminoAcid.comment: Includes alanine, leucine, valine, methionine, phenylalanine, tryptophan, and proline.
ex:NonPolarAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A NonPolarAminoAcid is an AminoAcid with a side chain that does not have any charge.

ex:PolarAminoAcidWithNoCharge.comment: Includes glycine, serine, threonine, cysteine, glutamine, asparagine, and tyrosine.
ex:PolarAminoAcidWithNoCharge.aristotelian_definition: A PolarAminoAcidWithNoCharge is an AminoAcid with a side chain that has polar groups but no charge.

ex:PolarAminoAcidWithPositiveCharge.aristotelian_definition: A PolarAminoAcidWithPositiveCharge is an AminoAcid with a side chain that has a positive charge.

ex:PolarAminoAcidWithNegativeCharge.comment: Includes aspartic acid and glutamic acid.
ex:PolarAminoAcidWithNegativeCharge.aristotelian_definition: A PolarAminoAcidWithNegativeCharge is an AminoAcid with a side chain that has a negative charge.

ex:AminoAcidSynthesisProcess.comment: This class covers various synthetic pathways for amino acids.
ex:AminoAcidSynthesisProcess.aristotelian_definition: An AminoAcidSynthesisProcess is a Process that involves the chemical reactions necessary to produce an amino acid from precursor molecules.

ex:CyanideAdditionReaction.comment: This reaction is part of the Gabriel synthesis method.
ex:CyanideAdditionReaction.aristotelian_definition: A CyanideAdditionReaction is a Process that involves the addition of cyanide to an aldimine, resulting in the formation of amino acids.

ex:PhthalimideSynthesisProcess.comment: This process is used in the preparation of certain amino acids.
ex:PhthalimideSynthesisProcess.aristotelian_definition: A PhthalimideSynthesisProcess is a Process that involves treating an alpha halogenated acid ester with potassium phthalimide to produce substituted phthalimides, which are then hydrolyzed to yield amino acids.

ex:NonStandardAminoAcid.comment: This class includes non-standard amino acids like D-Penicillamine.
ex:NonStandardAminoAcid.aristotelian_definition: A NonStandardAminoAcid is a MaterialEntity that does not conform to the standard set of 20 amino acids used in protein synthesis but has specific medical applications.

ex:DPenicillamine.comment: It is a metabolite of penicillin with specific medical applications.
ex:DPenicillamine.aristotelian_definition: DPenicillamine is a NonStandardAminoAcid that acts as a chelating agent and is used in the treatment of Wilson's disease.

ex:NAcetylcysteine.comment: It has various medical applications beyond amino acid synthesis.
ex:NAcetylcysteine.aristotelian_definition: N-Acetylcysteine is a NonStandardAminoAcid that functions as an antioxidant and is used in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency.

ex:Gabapentin.comment: It has specific medical uses unrelated to protein synthesis.
ex:Gabapentin.aristotelian_definition: Gabapentin is a NonStandardAminoAcid that acts as an anticonvulsant and is used in the treatment of epilepsy.
